name: Shadow Protocol
description: A web of espionage and betrayal spanning from Washington to Moscow.
seed_prompt: A spy thriller where operatives navigate shifting allegiances and deadly conspiracies.
lore_content:
The Cold War never really ended. It just went underground, into the shadows where deniable assets do deniable things.

Agent Sarah Cole, codename 'Specter,' is the CIA's best deep-cover operative. She's been playing a Russian oligarch's mistress for three years, feeding intel that's prevented two wars. Then her handler goes dark, and the agency claims they've never heard of her.

Viktor Volkov runs Russia's most secretive intelligence division, one that doesn't officially exist. A former KGB legend, he's been playing a long game that spans decades. His endgame involves a secret that would reshape the global order - if he can retrieve it before his rivals.

Director Elizabeth Hayes controls the NSA's Omega Division, a black-budget program tracking threats that don't appear in any briefing. She's discovered that someone inside the intelligence community is selling secrets to every side. The list of suspects includes people she trusts with her life.

Marcus Webb left MI6 after an operation went wrong in Syria. Now he runs security for tech billionaires and asks no questions. When his latest client is assassinated, Marcus finds himself holding a drive containing evidence of a conspiracy reaching the highest levels of multiple governments.

Dr. Anna Reyes designed the encryption system that protects NATO communications. She's just discovered a backdoor she didn't create - and tracing its origin has put her on someone's kill list. She has 72 hours to find help before the next attempt succeeds.

The Broker operates from a yacht that never stays in the same waters twice. They sell secrets to anyone who pays, but they have rules: no weapons of mass destruction, no children, no operations on US soil. Someone is framing them for breaking all three rules.

Zhang Wei is a Chinese MSS officer who's been feeding intel to the Americans for a decade. His handler just died in a suspicious accident, and his emergency contact leads to a dead drop that's been compromised. He has to decide: run, or find out who betrayed him.

origins.name: Deep Cover Operative
origins.description: You've spent years building a false identity, blending seamlessly into hostile environments.
traits: False Identity: You have a meticulously crafted false identity, including documents and contacts, granting advantage on checks to impersonate that identity. You also gain proficiency in the Forgery Kit.

origins.name: Intelligence Analyst
origins.description: You are trained to dissect information, identify patterns, and predict threats before they materialize.
traits: Deduction: You can spend 10 minutes analyzing a set of clues (written documents, surveillance footage, etc.) to gain advantage on your next Investigation check related to those clues.

origins.name: Special Forces Veteran
origins.description: You've seen the sharp end of combat, honed to peak physical and mental conditioning.
traits: Combat Conditioning: You have advantage on saving throws against exhaustion. You also gain proficiency with one type of weapon of your choice (firearm, heavy melee, etc.)

origins.name: Private Security Contractor
origins.description: You worked for private military organizations protecting the wealthy elite
traits: Tactical Awareness: You gain advantage on initiative rolls. Also, once per short rest, you can reroll a missed attack roll.

archetypes.name: Operative
archetypes.description: A master of infiltration and close-quarters combat, skilled in espionage and sabotage.

features.name: Sneak Attack
features.description: Beginning at 1st level, you know how to strike subtly and exploit a foe's distraction. Once per turn, you can deal an extra 1d6 damage to one creature you hit with an attack if you have advantage on the attack roll. The attack must use a finesse or a ranged weapon. The amount of the extra damage increases as you gain levels in this class, as shown in the Sneak Attack column of the Rogue table.

features.name: Cunning Action
features.description: Starting at 2nd level, your quick thinking and agility allow you to move and act quickly. You can take a bonus action on each of your turns in combat. This action can be used only to take the Dash, Disengage, or Hide action.

archetypes.name: Handler
archetypes.description: An expert in managing assets and extracting information from a network of contacts.
starting_equipment: A light pistol with one magazine
A cover identity complete with documents

features.name: Inspiration
features.description: You can inspire others through stirring words or music. To do so, you use a bonus action on your turn to choose one creature other than yourself within 60 feet of you who can hear you. That creature gains one Bardic Inspiration die, a d6. Once within the next 10 minutes, the creature can roll the die and add the number rolled to one ability check, attack roll, or saving throw it makes. The creature can wait until after it rolls the d20 before deciding to use the Bardic Inspiration die, but must decide before the GM says whether the roll succeeds or fails. Once the Bardic Inspiration die is rolled, it is lost. A creature can have only one Bardic Inspiration die at a time.

archetypes.name: Marksman
archetypes.description: A master of ranged combat and stealth, capable of taking down targets from extreme distances.
starting_equipment: A sniper rifle with scope and 20 rounds

features.name: Precise Shot
features.description: Once per turn, you can reroll an attack roll with a ranged weapon if the target is more than 60 feet away.

features.name: Keen Eye
features.description: You have advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight.

archetypes.name: Tech Specialist
archetypes.description: A brilliant mind specializing in electronics, software, and the intersection of technology and espionage.

features.name: Encryption
features.description: You have a deep understanding of Encryption; you gain advantage on checks relating to encryption or decryption.

features.name: Bug Sweeping
features.description: You can use 1 hour to sweep a room for listening devices. At the end of the hour, make an Intelligence check (DC 15) to discover listening devices.

setting_skills.name: Streetwise
setting_skills.description: Knowledge of the urban underground, including its contacts and hidden locations.

setting_skills.name: Technology
setting_skills.description: Knowledge of computer systems, networks, and hacking techniques.

setting_skills.name: Counterintelligence
setting_skills.description: Detecting espionage and rooting out enemy agents

world_descriptors.architecture: Glass-walled embassies, brutalist intelligence bunkers, anonymous safe houses, luxury hotel suites, underground parking garages
world_descriptors.landscape: Airport tarmacs at night, snow-covered Eastern European cities, Mediterranean ports, Swiss mountain passes, foggy London streets
world_descriptors.vegetation: Manicured embassy gardens, bare winter trees, potted plants in sterile offices, frozen forests
world_descriptors.weather: Cold rain, snowstorms, overcast European skies, Mediterranean heat haze, pre-dawn darkness
world_descriptors.people: Stone-faced operatives, elegant handlers, nervous assets, shadowy contacts, bureaucrats with classified access
world_descriptors.clothing: Tailored suits, tactical black, diplomatic formal wear, nondescript civilian covers, concealed holsters
world_descriptors.technology: Encrypted phones, surveillance equipment, hidden cameras, secure laptops, dead drop containers
world_descriptors.lighting: Interrogation spotlights, monitor glow in dark rooms, streetlights through rain, emergency exit signs, shadowed faces

visual_identity.visual_exclusions: Bright cheerful settings, casual vacation scenes, obvious weaponry displays, comic book action, family-friendly environments
